# 0x250 — `imu_accel`

DLC 8 · 100 Hz · status: **confirmed**

Three-axis accelerometer. Each axis is a 16-bit word with zero at about 7000 and about 992 counts per g.

## Layout

Bytes are numbered from 0. Multi-byte values are big-endian unless a row says otherwise. Bit 7 is the most significant bit of a byte.

| Byte | Content |
|---|---|
| B0 | `accel_x` |
| B1 | `accel_x` |
| B2 | `accel_y` |
| B3 | `accel_y` |
| B4 | `accel_z` |
| B5 | `accel_z` |
| B6 | `power_up_flags` |
| B7 | — |

## Signals

| Signal | Where | Type | Value | Unit | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accel_x` | B0:B1 | uint16 BE | raw × 0.001008 − 7.056 | g | confirmed (medium) |
| `accel_y` | B2:B3 | uint16 BE | raw × 0.001008 − 7.056 | g | confirmed (medium) |
| `accel_z` | B4:B5 | uint16 BE | raw × 0.001008 − 7.056 | g | confirmed (medium) |
| `lean_static` | B2:B3 | uint16 BE | raw × -0.057412 + 402.59 | deg | confirmed (high) |
| `power_up_flags` | B6 | uint8 | enum |  | hypothesis (medium) |

### `accel_x`

Longitudinal acceleration, (raw − 7000) / 992. Positive when the bike accelerates. 7000 is the nominal zero (the reset value); this bike reads about 7056 when level and at rest, which includes the mounting angle of the sensor.

**Confirmed by:** The derivative of wheel speed; GPS speed change.

**How we know:** Correlation 0.97 with the derivative of wheel speed over one ride; sign agrees with GPS speed change in 93 % of samples above 0.1 g on another.

**Caveats:** The zero is known to about ±20 counts (±0.02 g) and includes the mounting angle of the IMU.

**Example:** `0x250  1B B6 1B 37 1F CB 20 00` → 0.095 g

### `accel_y`

Lateral acceleration in the bike frame, (raw − 7000) / 992. The raw value falls when the standing bike is leaned to the left. In a balanced turn the bike leans into the resultant force, so this axis stays small: it moves a few counts per degree of lean in a corner (our estimates run from 2 to 4) against 17.4 counts per degree at standstill.

**Confirmed by:** An iPhone level (Measure app) fixed above the dash, filmed, bike parked.

**How we know:** 19 lean angles held at standstill against a phone inclinometer, R² 0.998.

**Example:** `0x250  1B B6 1B 37 1F CB 20 00` → -0.033 g

### `accel_z`

Vertical acceleration in the bike frame, (raw − 7000) / 992. About +1 g upright and at rest; rises above 1 g in a corner.

**Confirmed by:** Gravity: the magnitude of the three axes at rest.

**How we know:** Magnitude of the three axes at rest is 991-993 counts on six rides.

**Example:** `0x250  1B B6 1B 37 1F CB 20 00` → 1.148 g

### `lean_static`

Lean angle of a stationary bike from the lateral axis: (7012.3 − raw) / 17.418. Left is positive. Valid at standstill only; for a moving bike see docs/lean-reconstruction.md.

**Confirmed by:** An iPhone level (Measure app) fixed above the dash, filmed, bike parked.

**How we know:** Same 19-point standstill calibration as `accel_y`.

### `power_up_flags`

0x80 in the first frame, 0x60 for the next 0.4 s, then 0x20 for the rest of the session whether the bike moves or not. An earlier reading of bit 6 as a "moving" flag was wrong. B7 is always 0x00.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 32 | normal |
| 96 | first 0.4 s after power-up |
| 128 | first frame |

**Example:** `0x250  1B B6 1B 37 1F CB 20 00` → 32

> The first frame after power-up is the reset value `1B 58 1B 58 1F 40 80 00` (7000, 7000, 8000).
